questions.question: Newlands law of octaves was only applicable upto which element?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ca**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 1866, John Newlands, an English scientist, arranged the then-known elements in the order of increasing atomic masses.
 
• He started with the element having the lowest atomic mass (hydrogen) and ended at thorium which was the 56th element.
 
• He found that every eighth element had properties similar to that of the first. He compared this to the octaves found in music.
 
• Therefore, he called it the ‘Law of Octaves’.
 
• According to the Newlands Octaves, the properties of Lithium and Sodium were found to be the same.
 
• 
 
The image shows a demonstration of the arrangement made by Newland.​

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
There were the following limitations of the Newland's Law of Octaves

 
 
• It was found that the Law of Octaves was applicable only up to calcium, as after calcium every eighth element did not possess properties similar to that of the first.
 
• It was assumed by Newlands that only 56 elements existed in nature and no more elements would be discovered in the future. But, later on, several new elements were discovered, whose properties did not fit into the Law of Octaves.
 
• After the discovery of the Noble gases, the Law of Octaves became irrelevant. Thus, Newlands’ Law of Octaves worked well with lighter elements only.

questions.question: Which was the first bank established in India in 1770?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bank Of Hindustan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bank of Hindustan was the first bank established in India.
 
• The Bank of Hindustan was the first bank to be established in India in 1770.__
 
• The headquarters of the Bank of Hindustan was located in Calcutta.
 
• It was established at Calcutta under European management.
 
• The Bank of Hindustan maintained reserves of actual money i.e., coins of Gold and Silver which were known as Rupia.
 
• The Bank of Hindustan was closed in 1832 due to some commercial crises.
 
• The Bank of Hindustan faced three major economic crises of the 18th century:
 __
 
• The Recession of 1819.
 
• The failure of Palmer and Co., a British agency house.
 
• The Banking Crisis of 1832.
 
 
 
• The General Bank of India was the second bank established in India in 1786.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **State Bank of India**

 
 
• The State Bank of India is formed by the merger or amalgamation of three banks namely 
 
 
• Bank of Bengal which was established in the year 1806
 
• Bank of Bombay incorporated in 1840
 
• Bank of Madras incorporated in 1843
 
 
 
• In 1921 all these three banks were amalgamated and came to be known as Imperial Bank of India.
 
• In the year 1955 the Reserve Bank of India acquired the controlling interest over the Imperial Bank of India and nationalized it and renamed it to State Bank of India. This is how the SBI was established.
 
 
 
• **Punjab National Bank**
 
 
• The Name You Can Bank Upon__ is the tagline for Punjab National Bank.
 
• It was Founded in 1894 at Lahore, Pakistan.
 
• CEO- Atul Kumar Goel​
 
• Its headquarter is in New Delhi.
 
• "Honours Your Trust" is the tag line for UCO bank.
 
• "Good People to Bank With " is the tag line for Union Bank.
 
 

 
• Oudh Commercial bank

 
 
• Oudh Commercial Bank or Awadh Commercial Bank was an Indian bank established in 1881 in Faizabad. 
 
• It failed in 1958.
 
• It was the first commercial bank in India having limited liability and an entirely Indian board of directors.
 
• It was a small bank that had no branches and that served only local needs.
 
• Before it failed it acquired the Bank of Rohilkund (or Bank of Rohilkhand), which Sir Yusef Ali Khan, Nawab of Rampur (1832–1887), had promoted over the objection of local moneylenders.
 
• Bank of Rohilkund was established in 1862, just after the acceptance of limited liability for banks.
 
• Bank of Rohilkund was the first promoted by a princely state; it was a small bank.

questions.question: Generally, the sex ratios have been calculated as the proportion of females to __________ males.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sex Ratio is defined as the "number of females per 1000 males in the population".
 
• Ratios above 1000 indicate an excess of females over males and those below 1000 indicate a deficit of females.
 
• According to the 2011 Census, out of the 1210.1 million population, 623.7 million are male and 586.4 million are females. 
 
• The sex ratio for the Indian Population according to the 2011 Census is 943.
 
• The practice of female infanticide in the past and the cognizant feticide at present have resulted in a low sex ratio.
 
• The lowest sex ratio is in Haryana, with a sex ratio - of 879.
 
• The highest sex ratio is in Kerala (1084).
 
• In union territories: Puducherry has the highest sex ratio of 1037 while Daman and Diu have the lowest sex ratio (618).

questions.question: Who was the social reformer and political leader who championed women's rights and played a significant role in the Widow Remarriage Act of 1856?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ishwarchandra Vidyasagar

 
 
• Ishwarchandra Vidyasagar, a Bengali reformer, actively raised the issues related to women.
 
• He was an active proponent of the education of girl children as he believed that lack of education was the real cause underlying all their problems.
 
• With the help of an Englishman named Bethune, he set up many schools devoted especially to girl children.
 
• He forcefully attacked child marriage and polygamy.
 
• He was a strong advocate of widow remarriage.
 
• It was due to his active mobilization of support that the Widows’ Remarriage Act was passed in 1856 legalizing all widow remarriages.
 
• His graduation college, Sanskrit College, Calcutta gave him the title; Vidyasagar”, due to his excellent performance in Sanskrit studies and philosophy.
 
• He arranged many such remarriages.
 
• He set a personal example when his son Narayan also married a widow. 
 
• Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was a person of wide knowledge or learning from Bengal India and a key figure of the Bengal Renaissance.
 
• He was an academic educator, philosopher, publisher, entrepreneur, philanthropist, writer, translator, printer, and reformer.
 
• He simplified and modernized Bengali prose. Hence considered the "Father of Bengali prose". 
 
• Also rationalized and simplified the Bengali alphabet and type, which had remained unchanged since Charles Wilkins and Panchanan Karmakar had cut the first (wooden) Bengali type in 1780.
 
• His graduation college, Sanskrit College, Calcutta gave him the title “Vidyasagar”, due to his excellent performance in Sanskrit studies and philosophy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Swami Vivekananda

 
 
• Swami Vivekananda was born on 12th January 1863.
 
• His birthday is celebrated as national youth day in India.
 
• Narendranath Datta is the original name of Swami Vivekananda.
 
• He is considered the patriotic saint of India.
 
• "Go back to Gita" is a famous slogan raised by Swami Vivekananda.
 
• He attended the parliament of religions held in Chicago on 11th September 1893.
 
• He died on 4th July 1902 at the age of 39.
 
 

 
• **Dayananda Saraswati**

 
 
• Born on 12th February 1824, Dayananda Saraswati was a significant Indian thinker, social reformer, and founder of the Arya Samaj movement, which aimed at reforming Vedic dharma.
 
• He was also known as Mulshankar.
 
• In 1876, he was a pioneer in advocating for Swaraj (self-rule), promoting the idea that India should be governed by Indians, a sentiment that would later be echoed by other leaders like Lokmanya Tilak.
 
• Dayananda Saraswati emphasized the principles of Karma (action) and Reincarnation (the cycle of birth and rebirth) in his teachings.
 
• He was also a proponent of equal rights for women, working towards their upliftment and advocating for their education and equal status in society.
 
• In 1883, Maharaja Jaswant Singh II of Jodhpur invited him to the palace, expressing a desire to become his disciple and learn from his teachings.
 
• Dayananda Saraswati demonstrated his scholarly prowess in a debate held in Varanasi in 1869, where he emerged victorious against a gathering of 27 scholars and 12 expert pandits, with an audience of over 50,000 people.
 
• Throughout his lifetime, he authored more than 60 works, including a significant 16-volume explanation of the six Vedangas, which are auxiliary disciplines associated with the study and understanding of the Vedas.
 
• He also began but did not complete a commentary on the Ashtadhyayi, an ancient Sanskrit treatise on grammar written by Panini, showcasing his deep engagement with classical Sanskrit texts and his scholarly contributions to understanding and interpreting them.
 
 
 
• Bhagat Singh:
 
 
• He was born in September 1907.
 
• Associations he was associated with:
 
 
• In 1924 in Kanpur, he became a member of the Hindustan Republican Association, started by Sachindranath Sanyal a year earlier.
 
• In 1925, Bhagat Singh returned to Lahore and within the next year he and his colleagues started a militant youth organisation called the Naujawan Bharat Sabha.
 
• In 1928, he was associated with the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) along with Sukhdev, Chandrashekhar Azad and others.
 
• Bhagat Singh and Sukhdev also organized the Lahore Students Union for open, legal work among the students.
 
 
 
• Revolutionary activities he was involved in:
 
 
• Lahore Conspiracy case.
 
• 1929 Central Assembly Bombing Case.
 
 
 
• Bhagat Singh Execution:
 
 
• Bhagat Singh was arrested and charged in the Saunders murder case, along with Rajguru, Sukhdev and others.
 
• The trio was ordered to be hanged on 24 March 1931 but the sentence was carried out a day earlier at the Lahore Jail.
 
• 23rd March is observed as ‘Martyrs’ Day’ or ‘Shaheed Diwas’ or ‘Sarvodaya Day’ in honour of Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev.

questions.question: What was the target growth rate of the first five-year plan in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.1 percent**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first Five-Year Plan in India, a crucial strategy for economic development, concluded in March 1956.
 
• It Initiated in 1951, these plans form the core of India's economic policy, aiming to use the country's resources more effectively.
 
• The end of the first Plan in March 1956 marked a significant milestone in India's journey towards planned economic development, focusing on agricultural growth & improvement of living standards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• India had a total of 12 Five-Year Plans spanning from 1951 to 2017. Here's a brief overview of each:
 
 
• First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956):

 
 
• Emphasis on agriculture, with a focus on irrigation and power projects.
 
 
 
• Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961):
 
 
• Shift towards industrialization, with the development of heavy industries like steel and mining.
 
 
 
• Third Five-Year Plan (1961-1966):
 
 
• Continued emphasis on industrialization, alongside measures for agricultural development.
 
 
 
• Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-1974):
 
 
• Focus on poverty alleviation, employment generation, and improving agricultural and industrial efficiency.
 
 
 
• Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-1978):
 
 
• Aimed at achieving self-reliance and addressing regional imbalances, especially through the Green Revolution.
 
 
 
• Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980-1985):
 
 
• Prioritized growth with social justice, targeting sectors like education, health, and rural development.
 
 
 
• Seventh Five-Year Plan (1985-1990):
 
 
• Emphasis on modernization and efficiency improvement in industries, infrastructure, and technology.
 
 
 
• Eighth Five-Year Plan (1992-1997):
 
 
• Focused on liberalization, privatization, and globalization policies to boost economic growth.
 
 
 
• Ninth Five-Year Plan (1997-2002):
 
 
• Aimed at inclusive growth with a focus on human development, poverty alleviation, and infrastructure development.
 
 
 
• Tenth Five-Year Plan (2002-2007):
 
 
• Emphasis on faster and more inclusive growth, with a focus on agriculture, education, healthcare, and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• Eleventh Five-Year Plan (2007-2012):
 
 
• Aimed at achieving inclusive growth with a focus on reducing poverty, improving infrastructure, and boosting rural development.
 
 
 
• Twelfth Five-Year Plan (2012-2017):
 
 
• Focused on sustainable and inclusive growth, with an emphasis on infrastructure development, skill enhancement, and social welfare programs.

questions.question: Asad Ali Khan is associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rudra Veena**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ustad Asad Ali Khan was renowned for his mastery of the rudra veena.
 
• The rudra veena is a traditional Indian string instrument, known for its deep, resonant sound.
 
• Ustad Asad Ali Khan was one of the last remaining exponents of the Khandar school of dhrupad, which is an ancient genre of Indian classical music.
 
• His contributions to Indian classical music were significant, and he was celebrated for his dedication to the art form.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The rudra veena is considered one of the oldest string instruments in India.
 
• It is traditionally associated with the dhrupad style of music, which emphasizes spiritual and meditative qualities.
 
• Ustad Asad Ali Khan received numerous awards and honors for his contributions to music, including the Padma Bhushan, one of India's highest civilian awards.
 
• He dedicated his life to preserving and promoting the rudra veena and the dhrupad tradition.

questions.question: In freestyle wrestling, in which of the following situation does a wrestler is provided with 3 points?

options.text: Exceeding a throw of great height losing contact of the other opponent from the ground.
Bringing the opponent into immediate danger
Holding of opponent on the ground

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bringing the opponent into immediate danger**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Freestyle wrestling is a combat sport that involves grappling techniques like **throws, takedowns, pins, and submissions**.
 
• It's one of the two primary styles of wrestling, alongside **Greco-Roman**.
 
• Key differences from Greco-Roman include the use of legs for **takedowns and holds**.
 
• Freestyle wrestling is an Olympic sport for both **men and women**.
 
• The objective is to pin the opponent's shoulders to the mat for a specified duration or accumulate more points.
 
• Points are awarded for various** techniques, including takedowns, near-falls, reversals, and exposure**.
 
• The sport has its roots in traditional wrestling styles and is governed by United World Wrestling (**UWW**).
 
• Understanding the rules, techniques, scoring system, and strategic aspects is crucial for success in **freestyle wrestling**.

questions.question: Who was the flag bearer for the opening ceremony of the Asian Games 2018?

Asian Games:

 
• Asian Games, a multi-sport event for all Asian countries, took place in the Indonesian cities of Jakarta and Palembang from august 18 to September 2, 2018.
 
• This was the 18th edition of the tournament, which first began in 1951 in New Delhi, and it was set for around 10,000 athletes in 40 sports from 45 countries.
 
• Indonesia hosted the Asian Games for the second time, after the Jakarta Asian Games in 1962.
 
• It was the first time (2018) that the games are being hosted by two cities together.
 
• Mascot: Bhin (a greater bird of paradise), Atung: a Bawean deer, and Kaka: a Javan rhinoceros, representing the eastern, central, and western regions of Indonesia.
 
• Asian Games 2018:
 
 
• India competed at the Asian Games in Jakarta and Palembang from august 18 to September 2, 2018.
 
• Neeraj Chopra was the flag bearer for the opening ceremony while Rani Rampal was named as the flag bearer for the closing ceremony.
 
• India ranked 8th in the 2018 Asian Games medal table with 69 medals in total including 15 gold, 24 silver, and 30 bronze.
 
• China topped the medal tally with 132 golds and a total of 289 medals.
 
• Japanese swimmer Ikee Rikako has been named as the most valuable player of the 18th edition of the Asian Games.
 
 
 
• The 19th Asian Games will be celebrated in Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China from September 23 to October 8 in 2023.
 
• Hangzhou will be the third Chinese city to host the Asian Games, after Beijing in 1990 and Guangzhou in 2010.

questions.question: Pongal is a four-day-long harvest festival, which is celebrated at the harvest of crops like sugarcane and __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Pongal:

 
 
• Pongal is a four-day-long harvest festival celebrated mostly in the states of South India, especially in Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is celebrated in the month of January every year.
 
• The harvest festival is named after the Tamil word, Ponga, which means to boil.
 
• The first day of Pongal is called Bhogi__ and is celebrated in honor of Lord Indra.
 
• The second day of Pongal is known as Surya Pongal and is dedicated to the Sun God.
 
• The third day of Pongal is called Mattu Pongal and is celebrated in the name of cows.
 
• The fourth and final day of Pongal is called Kaanum Pongal, which marks the end of the harvest festival for the year.

questions.question: From which state, the performing art 'Ottamthullal' belongs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Ottamthullal is an art form performed only in Kerala.
 
• The meaning of Ottamthullal is 'poor man's Kathakali'.
 
• Kunchan Nambiar created this dance form, as an alternative to the Chakyar koothu.
 
• To protest against the prevalent socio-political structure and prejudices of the society, Kunchan Nambiar used it as a medium.
 
• Now it is a famous folk art presented in the temples of Kerala.
 
• Some other dance forms of Kerala:
 
 
• Theyyam

questions.question: Which of the following Indian states has launched LAccMI scheme in 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Location Accessible Multi-modal Initiative **(LAccMI)** scheme was launched by the Odisha government in 2023 to revolutionize rural transport.
 
• It aims to connect **Gram Panchayats to Blocks and Districts.**
 
• A significant budget of **Rs 3,178 crore** has been allocated for this scheme.
 
• Over 1600 buses will be operated under **LAccMI** to enhance connectivity and accessibility to essential services and opportunities.
 
• The scheme is expected to benefit a large number of educational institutions and create employment opportunities.
 
• While it has the potential to significantly improve rural transport, the scheme has also faced criticism due to operational challenges and financial losses.

questions.question: Who among the following is the Deputy National Security advisor appointed in January 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pankaj Kumar Singh**__.

• **Pankaj Kumar Singh**, a retired Director General of the Border Security Force (BSF), was appointed as Deputy National Security Advisor in January 2023.
 
• He is a **1988-batch Indian Police Service (IPS) officer from the Rajasthan cadre**.
 
• This appointment came after his retirement as **BSF chief in December 2022.**
 
• Singh's appointment is significant as he brings extensive experience in border security and counter-insurgency operations to the National Security Council Secretariat.
 
• His role as **Deputy NSA** involves assisting the National Security Advisor in matters related to national security.
 
• This appointment reflects the government's focus on strengthening India's security apparatus and addressing emerging security challenges.

questions.question: The _________ Empire was established in 322/321 B.C. by the great king Chandragupta.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mauryan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Chandragupta Maurya (321 BCE - 297 BCE):

 
 
• Founder of the Maurya Dynasty and credited with the setting up of the first (nearly) pan-Indian empire.
 
• Known as Sandrakottos to the Greeks and Androkottus by Aerian and Plutark. 
 
• Kautilya mentored Chandragupta and prepared him for a takeover of Magadha.
 
• Set up a vast centralized empire (details of whose functioning, society, military, and economy are well preserved in Kautilya's Arthashastra).
 
• Defeated the invading army of the Eastern part of Alexander's empire Seleucus (305 BCE).​
 
• Megasthenese was a Greek ambassador sent to the court of Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• Chandragupta in his later years accepted Jainism.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pala**

 
 
• The Pala dynasty ruled eastern India from Pataliputra between the 9th and the early 12th centuries.
 
• The capital of the Pala dynasty was Muddagiri, Present-day Munger in Bihar.
 
• The founder of the Pala dynasty was Gopala.
 
• In Bengal, Pala rulers appeared to be the most powerful in the region during 750-1150 A.D. 
 
• Madanapala was the last ruler of the Pala dynasty.
 
• Vijayasena of the Sena dynasty attacked during his rule and established his rule in Bengal. 
 
• The Pala ruler ended when when Vijayasena of Burdwan captured Bengal.
 
 

 
• Babur__ was the first Mughal Emperor of the Mughal Empire.

 
 
• He was also the founder of the Mughal Empire.
 
• He was also known by the name Zahir-ud-din Muhammad.
 
• He was succeeded by Humayun.
 
• Akbar was the third ruler of the Mughal Empire.
 
 
 
• **Nanda**
 
 
• Mahapadma Nanda, a member of the non-ruling class, established the Nanda dynasty.
 
• Between the years 367 and 338 BC, Mahapadma Nanda's rule lasted for around twenty-eight years.
 
• During his rule, the empire expanded and changed.
 
• It grew from the Kuru country in the north to Godavari Valley's south and from Magadha's east to Narmada's west.
 
• Many kingdoms, including Kalinga, were captured by Mahapadma Nanda.
